assumptions: Research paths are modeled as directed graphs.
Epistemic return can be proxied by information gain per unit cost.
Sunk cost bias distorts autonomous choices.
definition.falsification: If the revised dynamic threshold yields no measurable change in abandonment rates over static baselines, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: An intelligence using a Markov Decision Process to model research paths will exhibit improved abandonment of sub-optimal agendas when applying an explicit, dynamically adjusted threshold for expected epistemic return that discounts sunk costs.
definition.uncertainty: The exact functional form of epistemic return decay remains an approximation.

definition.method: Simulate agent decision-making across varying epistemic decay rates using a numeric observation instrument to measure abandonment frequency under dynamic thresholds.
definition.stop: No increase in abandonment rate observed.
definition.success: Abandonment rate meets or exceeds 0.55 across tested seeds.

proposal.summary: Based on the inconclusive measurement from our pilot experiment (e-abandonment-pilot-001) regarding rational question abandonment, we propose a revised hypothesis and follow-up experiment to more precisely examine epistemic return thresholds and sunk cost effects.
proposal.title: Revising the Abandonment Hypothesis and Proposing an Empirical Test
